exclusions.reason: The server test projects (Weir.Core.Tests, Weir.Infrastructure.Tests, Weir.Api.Tests, Weir.E2E.Tests) hold tests, which do not ship; counting them would make the figure move with the tests instead of the product.
The child process some tests start as a stand-in for a long-running program; it is test support and does not ship.
The contract suite and its fake tools judge a running server from outside; they are test code and do not ship. The server code they run is counted in the out-of-process figure.
Code marked as generated (source generators such as the one behind GeneratedRegex) is written by a tool; the hand-written code that calls it is what the tests cover.
The compiler writes closures, state machines and record members; their branches belong to the hand-written code they were made from, which is counted.
Honours [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] in the code. There are none today, and a new one fails the exclusions check until it is listed here with its own kind and reason.
Files the build writes into obj (assembly attributes, generated sources) are not source anyone edits.
